title: Clear Instructions, Context, and Constraints
subject: AI Foundations Day 36: Clear Instructions, Context, and Constraints

title: Prompting as Interface Design

summary: Learn how to think about prompts as a user interface for an AI system, so you can get clearer, more useful, and more reliable outputs.

title: Hallucinations: Why Fluent Can Still Be False

title: Generative AI across Text, Images, and Audio

title: Human Feedback and Preference Optimization

title: Fine-Tuning and Instruction Following
subject: AI Foundations Day 30: Fine-Tuning and Instruction Following

title: Next-Token Prediction and Emergent Capabilities

summary: Understand how modern language models learn broad language ability from huge text collections before any task-specific fine-tuning.

title: Tokens and Context Windows

title: Sequence Models before Transformers

title: Embeddings: Meaning as Geometry
subject: AI Foundations Day 23: Embeddings: Meaning as Geometry

title: Backpropagation: Assigning Credit for Error
subject: AI Foundations Day 21: Backpropagation: Assigning Credit for Error
summary: By the end of today, you will understand how a neural network learns from mistakes by tracing error backward through its layers and adjusting each weight a little bit in the right direction.

title: Layers, Activations, and Representations
subject: AI Foundations Day 20: Layers, Activations, and Representations
summary: understand what layers do inside a neural network, why activation functions matter, and how networks build representations step by step.

title: Neural Networks from First Principles
subject: AI Foundations Day 19: Neural Networks from First Principles
summary: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to explain how a neural network combines simple calculations into a flexible prediction system, what neurons, weights, layers, and activation functions do, and how training changes the network.

title: Probability, Calibration, and Confidence
subject: AI Foundations Day 18: Probability, Calibration, and Confidence
summary: Learn how to turn model outputs into useful probabilities, understand when “confidence” is trustworthy, and avoid common mistakes when interpreting prediction scores.

title: Decision Trees and Ensembles
subject: AI Foundations Day 17: Decision Trees and Ensembles
summary: By the end of today, you should understand how decision trees make predictions, why they are easy to interpret, and how ensembles combine many simple models into a stronger one.

title: Linear Models and Their Limits
subject: AI Foundations Day 16: Linear Models and Their Limits
summary: By the end of today, you will understand what a linear model is, when it works well, why it is so useful, and where it starts to fail.

title: Baselines: The Simplest Useful Benchmark
subject: AI Foundations Day 15: Baselines: The Simplest Useful Benchmark
summary: Learn how to build and use a baseline, compare your model against it, and avoid being fooled by numbers that look good but mean little.

title: Cross-Validation and Reliable Comparisons
subject: AI Foundations Day 14: Cross-Validation and Reliable Comparisons
summary: Learn how to estimate model performance more reliably, compare models fairly, and reduce the chance that one lucky split of data misleads you.

title: Confusion Matrices and Classification Tradeoffs
subject: AI Foundations Day 13: Confusion Matrices and Classification Tradeoffs
summary: Learn how a model’s classification mistakes break down in a confusion matrix , how to interpret the different kinds of errors, and how to choose a decision threshold that fits the real-world goal.

title: Evaluation Metrics That Match the Goal
subject: AI Foundations Day 12: Evaluation Metrics That Match the Goal
summary: Learn how to judge a model using metrics that actually reflect what you care about in the real world, so you can compare models fairly and avoid being fooled by a single number.

title: Optimization and Gradient Descent
subject: AI Foundations Day 11: Optimization and Gradient Descent
summary: By the end of today, you should understand how an AI model actually improves its predictions by repeatedly making small changes that reduce error.

title: Loss Functions: Defining What Wrong Means
subject: AI Foundations Day 10: Loss Functions: Defining What Wrong Means
summary: By the end of today, you’ll understand what a loss function is, why AI needs one, and how it turns “the model was wrong” into a number a machine can work with.

title: Features: Turning Reality into Inputs
subject: AI Foundations Day 9: Features: Turning Reality into Inputs
summary: By the end of today, you’ll understand what features are, how raw reality gets turned into machine-learning inputs, and how good feature choices can make a model much more useful.

title: Learning without Labels
subject: AI Foundations Day 8: Learning without Labels
summary: Understand how machines can learn useful structure from data when we do not tell them the correct answer for each example.

title: Classification, Regression, and Decision Boundaries
subject: AI Foundations Day 7: Classification, Regression, and Decision Boundaries
summary: By the end of today, you should be able to tell the difference between classification and regression , explain what a decision boundary is in plain language, and recognize when an AI system is making one kind of prediction versus the other.

title: Learning from Labeled Examples
subject: AI Foundations Day 6: Learning from Labeled Examples
